newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-EGGER FASTEST AFTER SLALOM FIRST LEG.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-EGGER FASTEST AFTER SLALOM FIRST LEG.

text.p: Sabine Egger of Austria turned in the fastest time for the first run of a women's World Cup slalom on Friday, while Pernilla Wiberg clinched her second title of the day before the race was completed.

Egger clocked 37.72 seconds on the Mammoth Mountain course to set the fast pace heading into the second leg. Wiberg was second fastest at 38.07, just two hundredths of a second quicker than Italy's Deborah Compagnoni.

But Sweden's Wiberg, who locked up the 1997 overall World Cup title with a third place super-g finish earlier in the day, nailed down the slalom crown when New Zealand's Claudia Riegler crashed near the top of the course.

Riegler came into the race second behind Wiberg in the slalom standings and was the only skiier with a chance to catch the Swede in the title hunt. Instead, Wiberg will head to the World Cup Finals in Vail next week with two titles already in her pocket.
Compagnoni can take over second place in the slalom standings with a strong second run Friday.
